Four dishes on a kitchen table seen so their insides show: a sandwich with cheese and tomato, a sandwich with chicken, a salad with egg and tomato, a soup with meat and potato; Ana lifts the bread of her sandwich to look inside.

lesson.title: 5.13 What's in it?
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.goal: Ask what is in a dish (What's in it? / What's in the soup?) and say what it holds (There's cheese and tomato in it.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.13 More Food: A1 names more foods (meat, cheese, vegetables, potato, tomato, salad, soup, sandwich) and says what you like and want; A1+ 5.13 asks what is inside a dish with What's in it? / What's in the …? and answers with A1+ 4.4's There's … in it, it standing for the dish (A1+ 4.11's it). Each photo shows one dish opened or from above so everything in it can be seen; every answer names all of it, so it fits one photo only. A1+ 4.15's any comes back in There isn't any chicken in it., told apart by ear.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.13 sandwich, salad, soup, cheese, tomato, meat, potato; A1 5.2 chicken, egg; A1+ 4.4 There's; A1+ 4.11 it; A1+ 4.15 any.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Join What's in it as one group (WHAT-sin-it) and keep in it short and joined (IN-it); do not require native-like speed.
